acts.title: Spring on the Heath
acts.blurb: Learn one thing at a time: clashes, Heralds, the Great Road, then Lore.

acts.title: Summer of Knives
acts.blurb: Three rivals at the table. Councils, the Favour and Deadly agents.

acts.title: The Long Winter
acts.blurb: The sharpest rivals, a boss rule in every crowning fight, and the Throne.

twists.how: Right after TB.newGame returns, set G.pl[bossSeat].lore = param (default 2); nothing else changes.
Pass order: [bossSeat, ...the other seats in random order] to TB.newGame so the boss starts first on the Order Track; later rounds re-sort by Influence as normal.
Right after TB.newGame returns, set G.fav = { h: bossSeat, u: 3 } so the boss starts holding the Favour disc with three uses instead of it lying on the Gleaning Meadow.
When the boss seat moves, call TB.AI.choose(G, bossSeat, 'hard', { budget: TB.AI.budgetMs * param }) so its rollouts get param times the normal thinking time (default 2).

intro.text: Three regions, three fights each round. Put a card face-down by each one.
When the cards flip, the bigger total takes the region and its Influence.
I keep the Court's gate. Come and knock, little heir, if you dare.

outro.text: Big card where it matters, small card where it doesn't. That is the whole trick.

opponent.name: Tamsin of the Gate
opponent.personality: Cheerful and careless; drops her cards wherever there is room.

goal.text: Win a short game (4 rounds) with more Influence than Tamsin.

easier.text: Tamsin plays even more loosely and every suggestion stays on.

intro.text: Before the fights, stand your Herald on one Location. Everyone can see it.
Win that region and pick that Location: +1 Influence, and 1 more from each rival there.
I will stand mine on the Cairn Field. Two Influence! Who could resist?

outro.text: Your Herald is a promise. Back it with your strongest card.

opponent.name: Tamsin of the Gate
opponent.personality: Always sends her Herald to the richest Location and forgets to defend it.

goal.text: Win, and collect your Herald Reward at least 2 times.

easier.text: Tamsin plays more loosely and the coach points at the best Location for your Herald.

intro.text: Each spring you bid one card. The highest bid picks first from the Great Road.
A Kingdom Card works every round, but the card you bid stays tucked under it.
The Choir collects what others leave behind. Bid low, friend. I'll wait.

outro.text: Two banners on your board already. The road remembers you now.
Remember: a bigger bid can steal a card you hold. Tuck a strong one.

opponent.name: Brother Fennick
opponent.personality: Patient and thrifty; bids his weakest card and hopes for scraps.

goal.text: Win, and end the game holding 2 Kingdom Cards.

stars.text: Steal a Kingdom Card with a bigger bid

easier.text: Fennick bids even more timidly, so the Great Road is nearly yours.

intro.text: In autumn you may Journey: send away a card with scrolls and gain that much Lore.
Spend Lore on your Site of Power. Those cards are stronger than anything you start with.
The heath pays toll to the Court. Every card you send away is one fewer to fight me.

outro.text: The toll is waived. This once. The Court will remember your face.
Spring is over. Now the other houses notice you.

opponent.name: Seneschal Halvard Crane
opponent.personality: Stiff and careful; defends the Cairn Field and never wastes a strong card.
opponent.taunt: Tolls are paid in full. Come back when your cards have grown teeth.
opponent.praise: Well. A heath-born heir with a Site of Power. Pass, and be welcome.

goal.text: Win, and buy at least 1 card from your Site of Power with Lore.

stars.text: Win and buy a Site of Power card

easier.text: Halvard plays more loosely, leaving you time to Journey and buy.

intro.text: Three houses at the table now. Each Council rewards cards with Votes on them.
In autumn, Govern: place one card with a Vote in the Council of Coin, Whispers or Pledges.
Votes are patient things, child. They pay long after the fighting is done.

outro.text: You voted, and the vote paid. Now you know why old women sit in councils.

opponent.name: Mother Quill
opponent.personality: Slow and calculating; fills the Councils and cashes in late.

goal.text: Win a 5-round game with 2 or more of your cards Governed into Councils.

intro.text: Win the Tablelands and take the Gleaning Meadow to claim the Kingdom's Favour.
The Favour gives your house a special action three times, and wins every tie.
My ferrymen already carry some Lore aboard. Catch us on the water if you can.

outro.text: Fair winds. I'll want that disc back before the summer's out.

opponent.name: Captain Rook Ashby
opponent.personality: Bold and fast; buys his Site of Power early and races for the Meadow.

twist.text: Rule: Captain Rook starts with 2 Lore.

goal.text: Win, and use your Favour action at least once.

stars.text: Hold the Favour disc at the end

easier.text: Rook starts with no extra Lore and plays more loosely.

intro.text: The Lantern Rising hide Deadly agents. When one flips, enemy cards in that clash die.
Deadly fails if any of your Followers stands there. Low cards can guard high ones.
You will never see my knife. Only the empty place where your champion stood.

outro.text: Unmasked by a heath-born upstart. My people will sing about it. Badly.
Summer ends. Winter brings the ones who want the Throne itself.

opponent.name: Sable, the Masked Heir
opponent.personality: Sly and theatrical; bluffs with Ruses, strikes with Deadly agents in the Sinks.
opponent.taunt: Every mask you tore off had another under it. Better luck in the dark.
opponent.praise: You read my masks like a printed broadsheet. Take the road north.

twist.text: Boss rule: Sable starts first on the Order Track in round 1.

easier.text: Sable loses the first seat and plays more loosely.

intro.text: Winter. The Court sends its best, and she counts every card you play.
One rival, four rounds, no mercy. The wall has never fallen.
Just the two of you, and a short year. Everything you've learned, used at once.

outro.text: The wall stands. You simply walked around it. I'll report that honestly.

opponent.name: Warden-General Ida Marsh
opponent.personality: Methodical and stubborn; samples every possible hand before she commits.

goal.text: Win a short game (4 rounds) against the Warden-General.

easier.text: Ida thinks less deeply about each move.

intro.text: The Choir has dreamt your every move. Twice over, and slowly.
Four houses now. Orlen thinks longer than anyone; give him nothing to read.
Shrine and Ossuary keep your deck fresh. Attrition shrinks the careless hand.

outro.text: The dream was wrong. How... refreshing. The Stag-King will want to meet you.

opponent.name: Orlen the Moth Priest
opponent.personality: Dreamy and unhurried; recycles the Lost Pile and outlasts everyone.

twist.text: Rule: Orlen takes twice as long to think through each big decision.

goal.text: Win a 4-player game with at least 14 Influence.

stars.text: Keep your Hand Size at 5 or more

easier.text: Three houses instead of four, and Orlen thinks at the normal pace.

intro.text: I have held the Favour since before your mother's mother. I will hold it at the end.
Six rounds, four houses. Ties go to the Favour, so take the Meadow or win clearly.
Whatever happens, child of the heath: you got here. Now take the chair.

outro.text: The thorns let you sit. They never let me. Rule kindly.
The Heathbound sit the Throne. Tell it slowly; we'll be singing it for years.

opponent.name: The Pale Stag-King
opponent.personality: Ancient and serene; hoards the Favour and wins on ties.
opponent.taunt: The Favour stays where it has always been. Kneel, and try another winter.
opponent.praise: The antlers bow. The Throne is yours, Heir of the Heath.

twist.text: Boss rule: the Stag-King starts holding the Kingdom's Favour (3 uses).

goal.text: Win a 6-round, 4-player game with at least 20 Influence.

stars.text: Hold the Favour disc at the end

easier.text: Five rounds, the Favour starts on the Meadow, and the rivals play at normal strength.
